advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Move the `dc_transport` fixture (and the store-copy/isolation fixtures) into `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` so `test_a_dc_issue_reaches_the_local_store_inbound` can resolve it instead of erroring at setup.
evidence: test_store_copy_isolation.py:249: `dc_store_copy_repo: Path, dc_transport: Any, jira_dc_project: str, track_issue: Any`
`dc_transport` is defined at test_transport.py:113 as `@pytest.fixture def dc_transport(jira_dc_pat: str)` — a module-local fixture, not in conftest.py
search of tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py and tests/external/conftest.py and tests/conftest.py for `def dc_transport` returned no matches, so it is not shared
By contrast jira_dc_project, jira_dc_pat, and track_issue ARE defined in tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py (lines 413, 432, 317) so they resolve; only dc_transport does not
advisory.finding: `test_a_dc_issue_reaches_the_local_store_inbound` requests the `dc_transport` fixture, which is defined only module-locally in `test_transport.py` (not in any conftest). Pytest does not share module-local fixtures across modules, so this test will error at setup with 'fixture dc_transport not found' rather than run.
advisory.suggested_fix: Promote `dc_transport` from test_transport.py into live_jira_dc/conftest.py (the ticket's file_impact already scopes the store-copy fixtures to conftest.py), so all modules in the directory can request it.

evidence: Ticket 5200-e04e-246e-4aae AC: 'the thin vertical slice (fetch + scrub + isolation + one inbound and one outbound round-trip) EXISTS AS ITS OWN INDEPENDENTLY-RUNNABLE TEST and is green'
Ticket Approach: 'land a vertical slice first: ... ONE inbound round-trip (create in DC, assert it appears locally) and ONE outbound round-trip (edit locally, assert it appears in DC)'

The module contains only test_a_dc_issue_reaches_the_local_store_inbound (line 248) and the dry-run plan test; there is no test that mutates a local ticket and asserts the change surfaces on a DC issue
Ticket AC: 'THIS is the epic's unproven half and the reason this story exists' — referring to the outbound (local edit -> DC) direction
advisory.finding: The module omits the OUTBOUND round-trip that the ticket's thin-slice acceptance criterion mandates. The docstring and commit describe 'one inbound round-trip', but the AC requires 'one inbound AND one outbound round-trip' (edit a local ticket, assert it surfaces on the DC issue); only the inbound test is present.

Sibling test_reconcile_pass.py:88-107 computes `_extra_missing_but_harness_up` and adds an autouse `_fail_if_extra_missing_while_harness_is_up` fixture that calls `pytest.fail(...)` precisely so 'harness up + extra absent' cannot silently skip; its docstring: 'J6 shipped two defects behind exactly that mask'
tests/external/conftest.py:26-37 `_jira_canary_should_fail` counts collected-vs-executed GLOBALLY per session, so a sibling's executing tests mask this module's all-skip
This module has no autouse loud-fail fixture (only `_skip` and `_skip_no_extra` marks)
advisory.finding: `_skip_no_extra` silently skips this whole module when the `[jira-datacenter]` extra is absent, dropping the sibling module's deliberate 'harness reachable but extra missing => LOUD FAILURE' guard. Because the session canary counts collected-vs-executed globally, a sibling module's executing tests mask this module's all-skip — the exact silent-skip mask the epic documents as having shipped two defects.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] In test_the_scrubbed_copy_plans_no_deletions_or_outbound_updates, assert the dry-run pass actually succeeded (returncode 0 and/or the `plan` key is present in the envelope) before treating an empty plan as evidence the scrub is clean.
evidence: tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_store_copy_isolation.py:288-289: assertions only check `deletions == []` and `updates == []` — both trivially true when `plan` is `[]`

reconcile.py:701-704: `if nowrite_plan is not None: ... result["plan"] = _build_plan_entries(mutations)` — the `plan` key is present ONLY on a successful no-write result, so a failed/errored pass omits it and `.get("plan", [])` masks the failure
ABSENCE: no assertion that the dry-run pass succeeded (no returncode check, no `"plan" in envelope` check, no error-envelope check) before concluding the scrub is complete
dropped.finding: test_the_scrubbed_copy_plans_no_deletions_or_outbound_updates can pass vacuously: `_envelope(cp).get("plan", [])` returns `[]` whenever the dry-run envelope has no `plan` key, which (per reconcile.py:701-704) is the case for any pass that did NOT complete a successful no-write run. The subprocess runs with check=False and the returncode/error state is never asserted, so an errored pass yields empty `deletions` and `updates` lists and BOTH assertions pass without the scrub ever being exercised.
dropped.suggested_fix: After `cp = _run_reconcile(...)`, add `assert cp.returncode == 0, cp.stderr` and `env = _envelope(cp); assert "plan" in env, f"pass produced no plan: {env}"`, then read `plan = env["plan"]` so an errored/plan-less envelope fails loudly instead of passing vacuously.
